lenses.dreamBook: Stairs going down: a time of reflection before a change. An old family house: news from family, or a return to an old question. Hearing your name called: an important message is near, so listen to the people close to you this week.
lenses.psychology: Endless stairs in a familiar house often appear when you are working through something slowly, one step at a time, without seeing where it ends. Your grandmother’s house points to roots and safety. The voice calling from below is a part of you asking for attention - a feeling or a decision you keep postponing.
lenses.spiritual: Going down stairs is a classic image of a journey inward, toward memory and intuition. A house that keeps growing suggests your inner world is larger than you let yourself explore. The calling voice is often read as guidance: something from your past holds wisdom for your present.

200.description: One of the most common dreams there is. Teeth are how we bite into the world and how we smile at it, so losing them often shows up when you feel you are losing grip on a situation, or worry about how others see you.

lenses.dreamBook: Teeth falling out: worry that will pass. One tooth: news from a relative. Teeth growing back: recovery after a loss. Painless loss: a change you will be glad of later.
lenses.psychology: Losing teeth tends to appear in periods of pressure about control or appearance: a new job, a conflict, a moment of being watched. The anxiety is real, but it is about confidence, not about your health.
lenses.spiritual: Teeth falling away can mark the end of an old way of holding on. Something you gripped tightly is ready to be released, making room for a softer, more honest way of meeting the world.

200.question: Where in your life do you feel less in control than you would like?
200.title: Teeth falling out
